react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by a compact steroid hormone cluster: dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), androstenedione, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone (DHT), estrone, and 17β-estradiol. Cross-paradigm consensus identifies androgen and estrogen metabolism as the single overwhelming winner. In RaMP multi-DB ORA, the KEGG map00150 / SMPDB SMP00068 entry "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" ranks #2 with FDR 5.8×10⁻¹⁸, fold-enrichment 1501, and all six steroids present; the parent Reactome pathway "Metabolism of steroid hormones" (R-HSA-196071) follows at FDR 5.1×10⁻¹⁷. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as top hit (p = 5.77×10⁻⁷). The mummichog m/z-direct network analysis, using the empirical-compound human_mfn graph, independently recovers the same biological signal as its top two hits: "C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism" (p = 8.4×10⁻⁵) and "Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism" (p = 3.4×10⁻⁴), both with 14–15 matched metabolites including every input steroid. Four additional WikiPathways entries (WP496 "Steroid biosynthesis", WP2263 "Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer", WP5368 "Sulfatase and aromatase pathway", WP4523 "Classical pathway of steroidogenesis") achieve FDR < 1.6×10⁻¹⁶ in RaMP, all converging on the same steroid biosynthetic nodes. The six driver steroids share the C19/C18 sterane scaffold and map to the sequential enzymatic steps: CYP17A1 (DHEA from pregnenolone), HSD17B (androstenedione ↔ testosterone), SRD5A2 (testosterone → DHT), and CYP19A1 (androstenedione → estrone → estradiol). The non-steroid metabolites (caffeine, sucrose, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl) appear as peripheral singletons without consistent pathway membership. ID reconciliation confirmed all 11 input metabolites as structurally distinct with unique InChIKey first-block hashes, ruling out namespace artefacts. The biological interpretation is that the treatment perturbs steroidogenesis at multiple enzymatic steps, simultaneously elevating C19 androgens and C18 estrogens in a pattern consistent with aromatase induction or CYP17A1 up-regulation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA lists KEGG:map00150 "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" as its top hit with FDR 5.8×10⁻¹⁸ and six matched metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers KEGG:hsa00140 at p=5.8×10⁻⁷ with the same six steroid metabolites. The mummichog m/z-direct network analysis identifies MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as the top pathway at p=8.4×10⁻⁵, with all six steroids appearing in its matched compound roster. RaMP also returns REACT:R-HSA-196071 "Metabolism of steroid hormones" at rank 5 with FDR 5.1×10⁻¹⁷. The six driver metabolites—dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), androstenedione (C00280), testosterone (C00535), dihydrotestosterone (C03917), estrone (C00468), and 17β-estradiol (C00951)—are confirmed as members of each of these pathways. Caffeine, sucrose, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl are peripheral singletons absent from these pathway hits.

Reactome REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) independently recovers the same six steroids at FDR=5.1×10⁻¹⁷. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm returns MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism and MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism both at p=8.4×10⁻⁵, with perfect 14-of-14 and 15-of-15 overlap respectively, confirming the signal at the network level. WikiPathways WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis) captures five of the six steroids with FDR=1.6×10⁻¹⁶. Sucrose independently hits the disaccharide metabolism cluster (Starch and Sucrose Metabolism, Galactose metabolism) via mummichog at p=0.046.
